title: Not one who has not turned from wrong
theme: Not one who has not ceased from bad conduct, nor one who is not calm, not collected, nor one whose mind is not at peace, can reach him by knowledge.

words.meaning: one whose mind is not at peace

sandhi.rule: a + a → ā, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः); aḥ → o before a voiced consonant, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च); a final t before n becomes n, P. 8.4.45 (यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा).
a + a → ā and ā + a → ā, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः); aḥ → o before v, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च).

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi; m before a vowel
sandhi.rule: a + e → ai, P. 6.1.88 (वृद्धिरेचि); final m stays before a vowel.

samasa.meaning: one whose mind is not at peace

morphology.note: Optative 3 sg. of āp ‘reach, obtain’: ‘would attain’, a statement of possibility; the four negated subjects each take it.
Enclitic pronoun ‘him’, referring back to the self of the preceding verses.
mānasa ‘mind’ (a derivative of manas); Madhva’s text has manas itself, aśāntamanasaḥ, with the same sense.

translation.literal: ‘Not one who has not ceased from bad conduct, not one not calm, not one not collected, nor even one whose mind is not at peace, would attain him by knowledge.’
translation.readable: ‘No one who has not turned away from wrongdoing, who is restless, who is scattered, or whose mind is not at peace, can reach the self through knowledge.’

anvaya: दुश्चरितात् अविरतः न, अशान्तः न, असमाहितः न, अशान्तमानसः वा अपि न प्रज्ञानेन एनम् आप्नुयात् ॥
syntax: Four negated subjects, each introduced by na (nāvirato …, nāśānto, nāsamāhitaḥ, nāśāntamānaso), share one verb, āpnuyāt, with prajñānena as instrument and enam as object. Śaṅkara and Raṅgarāmānuja both restate it positively: the one who has ceased, is calm, collected and at peace does reach him.

ambiguities.topic: How do aśānta and aśāntamānasa differ?
ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: aśānta is one not restrained from the restlessness of the senses, «इन्द्रियलौल्यात् अशान्तः»; aśāntamānasa one who, though collected, is still anxious for the fruit of concentration, «समाहितचित्तोऽपि सन्समाधानफलार्थित्वात् नापि अशान्तमानसः». Raṅgarāmānuja: one whose surges of desire and anger are not quieted, «अनुपशान्तकामक्रोधवेगः», and one whose mind is not restrained.

Madhva’s text reads prajñānenaivam āpnuyāt, ‘would attain [it] so’, for prajñānenainam, ‘would attain him’ (corrections.json, variant). Śaṅkara’s paraphrase of the positive sense also says ‘thus’, «प्रज्ञानेन एवं यथोक्तमात्मानं प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः», after glossing enam in the lemma.

beginner: After saying that cleverness and learning are not enough, the Upaniṣad says what is needed. A person who has not stopped doing wrong cannot reach the self, nor can someone whose senses are restless, whose attention is scattered, or whose mind is not at peace. Knowledge alone, without this, does not get there. Śaṅkara explains each condition: give up forbidden actions, quiet the craving of the senses, gather the mind to one point, and stop worrying even about the results of that concentration. He adds that the person who does all this, with a teacher, reaches the self. Raṅgarāmānuja treats these virtues as part of the practice of worship: someone who ignores ordinary morality cannot make that practice whole.
analogy: Like trying to see the bottom of a pond: no instrument helps while the water is still being stirred.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: That no one who has not ceased from wrong conduct, who is not calm, not collected, or whose mind is not at peace, can reach the self by knowledge.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: A positive restatement: the one who has turned from wrong conduct and from the restlessness of the senses, whose mind is collected and at peace even about the fruit of concentration, and who has a teacher, reaches the self, «समाहितचित्तः समाधानफलादप्युपशान्तमानसश्चाचार्यवान्». Prajñāna is knowledge of Brahman, «ब्रह्मविज्ञानेन».

commentary.q: Why are moral rules made part of meditation?
commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: Raṅgarāmānuja: the verse teaches certain virtues as auxiliaries of the worship that leads to the Supreme, «परमात्मप्राप्तिहेतुभूतोपासनाङ्गतया कांश्चिद्धर्मान् उपदिशति». Just as the general rule against lying is also enjoined within a particular rite, abstaining from wrong conduct is enjoined as part of worship; whoever ignores it, its defect leaves the worship incomplete.

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: Madhva gives the verse without comment in our source; his text reads aśāntamanaso for aśāntamānaso and prajñānenaivam for prajñānenainam (corrections.json).

advaita.text: Knowledge of Brahman reaches the self only in one prepared by restraint, concentration and a teacher: «समाहितचित्तः समाधानफलादप्युपशान्तमानसश्चाचार्यवान्».

visistadvaita.text: Moral restraint is an auxiliary of the worship that attains the Supreme: «परमात्मप्राप्तिहेतुभूतोपासनाङ्गतया कांश्चिद्धर्मान् उपदिशति».

schools.disagreement: Both make ethical and mental preparation a condition of knowing; Śaṅkara treats it as preparing the mind for knowledge of Brahman, Raṅgarāmānuja as a component of the worship that wins the Lord. Madhva does not comment here in our source.

parallels.note: Yājñavalkya’s list — calm, restrained, withdrawn, patient, collected — of those who see the self in the self.

parallels.quote: नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो न च प्रमादात्तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात्
parallels.note: The Muṇḍaka’s counterpart: the self is not reached by one without strength, nor through negligence.

contemporary.text: It is tempting to treat understanding as a matter of information. The verse says that how one lives — whether one has stopped harming, whether the mind can settle — decides what one is able to see. (A modern reflection.)

reflect.beginner: Have you noticed that you think less clearly when you are doing something you know is wrong?
reflect.deeper: Why might Śaṅkara add that the seeker must be calm even about the fruit of concentration?
reflect.practice: For one day, notice each time the mind is pulled by a sense craving, and simply let it pass.

flags.note: Madhva’s text reads nāśāntamanaso and prajñānenaivam āpnuyāt (corrections.json, variants).
